title: Adaptive priority respite windows for tenant bursts during limiter degradation
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Problem: During intermittent limiter outages and global congestion events we observe disproportionate impact on high-priority tenants and noisy low-priority tenants simultaneously attempting large bursts. Existing emergency shedding is binary and causes latency spikes and SLO breaches for priority customers. This ticket proposes an adaptive 'priority respite window' mechanism combined with soft-probing admission tokens to gracefully absorb bursts, maintain tenant fairness, and support multi-region circuit-breaker choreography when quota proxies are degraded.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Priority respite windows allow high-priority tenants to consume short-term excess capacity during limiter degradation without violating global SLOs.
2) Soft-probing reduces synchronized retries by staggering retry admission; simulated burst tests show 40-60% lower tail latency compared to current emergency-shedding baseline.
3) Cross-region circuit-breaker coordination prevents double-counting of respite capacity during regional failover (integration test passes).
4) Monitoring dashboards expose per-tenant respite usage, missed-respite events, and adjusted token-balance metrics.
5) Rollout executed as opt-in feature behind a runtime flag and no customer data is persisted outside existing audit logs.
6) Benchmark: under the synthetic tenant-burst workload, 99th percentile latency for P0 tenants does not exceed current SLO by more than 10% during a limiter degraded window.
7) Documented failback behavior: when limiter heals, respite allowances are reconciled deterministically and no tenant receives cumulative >1.5x of normal steady-state quota within 1 hour.
implementation_notes: Design a respite token bucket per tenant class (P0/P1/P2) with a short TTL window and emergency-weight that is drawn only when admission detects degraded limiter health.
Introduce 'soft-probing' admission path: small lightweight probes from queued requests that inform global admission controller of actual capacity; probes are randomized to avoid stampedes.

Coordinator: extend the existing quota proxy to publish a compact 'respite ledger' across regions via the routing plane (use existing lease stream; fall back to per-region conservative estimates on partition).
Circuit-breaker choreography: on region-blind failover, proxies must reconcile respite consumption using monotonic sequence IDs to avoid double-granting; include tombstones for drained leases.
Add deterministic reconciliation logic that drains temporary respite tokens gradually when normal quota returns; log all grants to existing audit stream for compliance.
Implementation will be feature-flagged with k8s rollout: step 1 proxy-only logic, step 2 runtime routing-awareness, step 3 console toggle for tenant opt-in.
Spike work done: microbenchmarks for token checks show ~200ns added in the hot path when feature disabled; target <1us when enabled with fast path caching.
testing_plan: Unit tests for respite ledger encoding/decoding and TTL expiration semantics.
Integration tests for cross-region reconciliation using recorded-wire tests (simulate split-brain and rejoin).
Load tests: multi-tenant synthetic bursts (50k rps across mixed tenants) with and without limiter degradation to measure tail latency, fairness index, and token utilization.
Chaos tests: kill quota proxy pods and verify that respite coordination prevents priority SLO regressions; validate rollback pathways.
Canary rollout to staging alpha customers (internal and 3 pilot tenants) with telemetry enabled for 48 hours before broader rollout.
Benchmark acceptance: automated perf jobs must show improved P0 tail latency or equivalent cost savings compared to baseline within noise margin.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tenant respite consumption heatmap, global respite burn rate, 99/999 latency during respite windows.
Alerts: respite_missed rate > 0.5% for P0 tenants over 5m => Pager; reconciliation_lag > 120s during normal ops => Oncall.
SLO instrumentation: tag requests served via respite to enable post-hoc quality analysis and regression detection in Optimize.
Audit logs: every respite grant emits audit event to existing centralized audit stream (for compliance).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev and staging testing behind feature flag; no customer traffic.
Phase 1: enable proxy-only logic in multiregion staging; run synthetic burst scenarios and validate reconciliation.
Phase 2: opt-in pilot with 3 trusted tenants (low-risk customers); monitor metrics and collect feedback for 2 weeks.
Phase 3: gradual enable for all tenants with flag off by default but auto-enable for P0 tenants under emergency operator approval.
Phase 4: full launch with console controls for tenant-level respite thresholds and opt-out knob.
Rollback: disable feature flag and run reconciliation job to drain outstanding respite tokens deterministically.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Double-granting respite tokens across regions under partition could inflate total capacity. Mitigation: sequence IDs and conservative local caps; on reconciliation, excess grants are revoked via compensating drains.
Risk: Noisy low-priority tenants gaming respite windows. Mitigation: realtime fairness filter and adaptive decay that penalizes rapid repeated grants.
Risk: Increased control-plane chatter may add latency. Mitigation: compact ledger messages, backoff, and prefer eventual reconciliation rather than synchronous global locks.
Risk: Compliance/audit concerns about temporary elevated allowances. Mitigation: every grant is recorded in audit stream; provide tenant-visible audit report in Console.
